stories.title: Jags' home winning streak against Indy is 'weird, quirky' and a long shot to end Sunday
stories.summary: — Jaguars left tackle Walker Little perfectly summed up Jacksonville's 11-game home winning streak against Indianapolis.
stories.detail: JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- — Jaguars left tackle Walker Little perfectly summed up Jacksonville's 11-game home winning streak against Indianapolis. “It’s one of those weird, quirky stats that you see and you’re like, ‘That’s crazy,’” Little said. It has been an annual storyline surrounding this AFC South matchup for years — and might very well still be in 2027. The Jaguars (4-2), fresh off a bye week, will try to extend the streak when they host the struggling Colts (2-5) on Sunday. Indianapolis last won at EverBank Stadium in 2014 and will try to end the skid after a trying week in which the Colts traded team captain DeForest Buckner and longtime guard Quenton Nelson to start a rebuilding effort. “Regardless of circumstances, we have a job to do, and we’re excited for that challenge,” Colts coach Shane Steichen said. Indianapolis has dropped three in a row and 12 of 14 dating to last season. The Colts’ futility on the road against Jacksonville might be even more of a head-scratching slump. The 11-game slide includes a trip to London in 2016. Even in some of the Jaguars’ worst years — a one-win campaign in 2020 and a pair of three-win seasons — they managed to beat Indianapolis at home…

stories.title: Falcons' Penix and Buccaneers' Mayfield aiming to help rebounding teams take control of NFC South
stories.summary: — Welcome to the NFC South, where inconsistency and seemingly disastrous starts to this season have not undermined the aspirations of the Atlanta Falcons and Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
stories.detail: TAMPA, Fla. -- — Welcome to the NFC South, where inconsistency and seemingly disastrous starts to this season have not undermined the aspirations of the Atlanta Falcons and Tampa Bay Buccaneers . After all, it is a division won by teams finishing with losing records two of the past four seasons, including a year ago when Carolina, the Falcons and Bucs all went 8-9. The Panthers by tiebreaker claimed their first title since 2015 and currently sit atop the standings again with a 3-3 record. Atlanta (3-4) and Tampa Bay (2-5) are lurking despite slow starts, with each hoping to bolster bids to take control of a wide-open race when the rivals meet Sunday. With Michael Penix Jr . at quarterback, the Falcons have won three of five following an 0-2 start that included a 31-point loss at Carolina. The third-year pro, who missed much of lase season with a knee injury, is coming off throwing for three touchdowns without an interception in a 29-20 victory over previously unbeaten San Francisco. The Bucs dropped four straight to begin the season, but are feeling better about themselves after riding a rejuvenated defense and relentless rushing attack to win two of their past three. stories.title: Jets' Brownlee says he was benched for missing meetings, but 'good' for Sunday
stories.summary: Jets nickelback Jarvis Brownlee Jr. was benched last Sunday because he missed multiple mandatory meetings and was fined by the team.
stories.detail: FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- New York Jets nickelback Jarvis Brownlee Jr . was benched last Sunday because he missed multiple mandatory meetings and was fined by the team, he told ESPN on Thursday. Brownlee said he couldn't recall the amount of the fine, except to say he was notified in a letter from the team. He said he missed "more than one" meeting, adding that he understood the discipline. "No doubt, no doubt," he said. "Just accountability." Asked why he missed the meetings, Brownlee said, "It was just something in-house, some things I had to get right." Brownlee, the Jets' starting nickel, was inactive for the New York's 28-25 loss to the Miami Dolphins . He was replaced by rookie D'Angelo Ponds . Coach Aaron Glenn declined to say why he benched Brownlee, adding that he wanted to keep the reason "in-house." Brownlee said he's "good" for this week. From indications, he will be active Sunday when the Jets (2-5) host the Las Vegas Raiders (3-4). The Jets acquired Brownlee from the Tennessee Titans early in the 2025 season. The Jets traded a 2026 sixth-round pick for Brownlee and a 2026 seventh-round pick. Brownlee, a 2024 fifth-round pick by Tennessee, has appeared in 13 games for the…

stories.title: Cowboys look for rare winning streak under Brian Schottenheimer in visit from Cardinals
stories.summary: — Sustainability is the next challenge for the Dallas Cowboys, who have just one winning streak in nearly a season and a half under coach Brian Schottenheimer.
stories.detail: ARLINGTON, Texas -- — Sustainability is the next challenge for the Dallas Cowboys , who have just one winning streak in nearly a season and a half under coach Brian Schottenheimer. Dallas (3-4) begins a stretch of four home games in five weeks with a visit from Arizona on Sunday after a 38-21 road division win against two-time defending NFC East champion Philadelphia. As strange as it sounds, the Cowboys did what they should have against the Eagles. Philadelphia's offense is decimated by injuries, and the beleaguered Dallas defense still needed three quarters to figure out how to get stops. The Cowboys had the second-worst rushing offense in the NFL before Javonte Williams went for a career-high 155 yards rushing among the team's 204. A two-week rut ended for one of the league's best offenses, with season highs in yards and points. Now Dallas has to do it again. “It’s a business where you have to be consistent with your execution, with your performance,” said Schottenheimer, whose only winning streak was a three-game run last season. “And I think we've been lacking that at times. stories.title: Cowboys add OG Tyler Smith, TE Luke Schoonmaker to their injury report
stories.summary: The Cowboys added two players to their injury report and opened the 21-day practice window for defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard (calf).
stories.detail: The Cowboys added two players to their injury report and opened the 21-day practice window for defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard (calf). Bullard was a full participant. Left guard Tyler Smith (ankle) was also a full participant. He was not on Wednesday's injury report. Tight end Luke Schoonmaker (groin) also wasn't on the injury report Wednesday. He was a non-participant Thursday. The rest of the Cowboys' report remained the same. Cowboys defensive back Caleb Downs (ankle), wide receiver George Pickens (shoulder/hamstring) and defensive tackle Quinnen Williams were limited participants again Thursday. Pickens played only 41 of 68 offensive snaps on Monday night, while Downs was in on 56 of 66 defensive snaps and Williams on 38. Offensive tackle Drew Shelton (hamstring) was the team’s other limited player. Wide receiver KaVontae Turpin (ribs) and linebacker Dee Winters (calf) remained out of practice. Outside linebacker Marist Liufau (forearm) and safety P.J. Locke (foot) both appear ready to return. They are in their 21-day return-to-practice windows.

One of six teams to put in a waiver claim on former Las Vegas Raiders defender Jonah Laulu, they were undone by their record being superior to that of the other five potential claimants. Besides the Patriots, the Tennessee Titans, Miami Dolphins, Houston Texans, Indianapolis Colts and New York Jets also tried to bring Laulu on board, according to a report by NFL insider Jordan Schultz. The 1-5 Titans were awarded the 26-year-old on Wednesday. Laulu entered the league as a seventh-round draft pick by the Colts in 2024 but was waived after his rookie training camp. He ended up with the Raiders as a waiver claim, and since then played 39 games with 22 starts for Las Vegas. Along the way, he registered 5.5 combined sacks — including 0.5 in five games this season. stories.title: Knicks to decline Pacome Dadiet's fourth-year option
stories.summary: The Knicks are set to decline Pacome Dadiet's fourth-year option, making the former first-round pick an unrestricted free agent in June.
stories.detail: The Knicks are planning to decline former first-round pick Pacome Dadiet 's fourth-year option, SNY's NBA Insider Ian Begley confirms. New York's move will make Dadiet an unrestricted free agent next June and create salary space heading into the 2027-28 season. Dadiet, who was selected 25th overall in the 2024 NBA Draft, has been unable to carve out playing time with the Knicks since he arrived. The French national appeared in 18 games his rookie season, where he averaged 1.7 points on 32 percent shooting. He averaged the same amount of points on 33 percent shooting across 29 games last season. This season, the 21-year-old has appeared in one game, grabbing one board in his one minute on the court.

stories.title: LeBron James looked all 41 years of his life on these highlight plays
stories.summary: LeBron James was on the wrong end of a crossover and chasedown block to finally look old
stories.detail: LeBron James is essentially outlasting every elite athlete in the history of sports by playing his 24th season for the Philadelphia 76ers this year. James turns 42 years old in Dec., and if he fulfills the second year of his contract next season, he will have played 10 more seasons than Michael Jordan. James’ peak wasn’t as high as MJ’s by most models , but he’s trying to win the GOAT debate on longevity, and he’s certainly made it a worthwhile discussion. Father Time doesn’t lose, and that’s even the case against a freak of nature like LeBron. James showed some signs of age on Wednesday night as his 76ers needed a big fourth quarter comeback just to get by the Indiana Pacers without Tyrese Haliburton and Ivica Zubac. James was solid in the win with 13 points, 10 assists, five rebounds, and three stocks, but he was also on the wrong end of two highlight plays that the internet is still talking about a day later. Early in the second quarter, James was speeding down the court for what should have been a fastbreak dunk. Instead, Indiana’s Jalen Slawson, who is only on a two-way contract, beat him to the rim for the chasedown block. He did a LeBron to LeBron! Watch the play here: JALE…

stories.title: Timberwolves' Anthony Edwards undergoes successful knee scope
stories.summary: Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards underwent a "successful" arthroscopic procedure on his ailing right knee at the Mayo Clinic on Thursday, the team announced.
stories.detail: Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards underwent a "successful" arthroscopic procedure on his ailing right knee at the Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota, on Thursday, the team announced. Edwards had a debridement procedure performed on his knee, which is a minimally invasive measure used to clean, smooth or remove damaged cartilage, bone spurs or loose joint fragments from the knee joint to relieve pain and improve mobility, according to the Mayo Clinic. The team's statement said Edwards is expected to make a full recovery but did not denote a time frame for his potential return. Sources told ESPN's Shams Charania that Edwards could be sidelined up to two months . Speaking before Wednesday night's loss to the Warriors, Timberwolves president of basketball operations Tim Connelly said he expects Edwards to be "good as new" when he eventually returns to game action . Edwards, 25, has been bothered by right knee pain since last spring and was limited to a career-low 61 games last season. He was seen grabbing his knee and grimacing at one point during Sunday's home opener against the Toronto Raptors . teamStories.detail: Welcome to the final days of October, featuring falling leaves, early sunsets, Halloween decorations illuminating the night -- and the yearly pastime of overreacting to the first week of a new NBA season . Charlotte is already better without LaMelo Ball ! Ty Jerome ? Ty Jerome!
